chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعًا، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all together, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: إِنَّ مِنْ عَرَائِفِ الْفِقْهِ الْحِلْمُ وَالصَّمْتُ

translations.en: Indeed, among the signs of understanding (fiqh) are forbearance and silence.

en.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies forbearance (hilm) and silence (samt) as key indicators of deep religious understanding (fiqh). This teaching emphasizes that true knowledge is manifested not just in intellectual capacity but in ethical conduct and restraint.
en.seo_question: What are the primary signs of true religious understanding (fiqh) according to Imam al-Rida?

key_terms.الْحِلْمُ: forbearance, gentleness, patience in the face of provocation
key_terms.وَالصَّمْتُ: and silence, quietness, restraint of speech
